grade.first_issue: In Case 2, the claim that the proposed limiting distribution minimizes \(A\) for every fixed \(p\) is unsupported; the accompanying monotonicity discussion does not establish that losses among triples containing \(x_1\) are compensated elsewhere.
grade.summary: The construction proving attainability of \(136\) is correct, as are several special cases. However, the lower bound for the central range \(2\le p\le15\) rests entirely on an unproved extremal assertion. A new load-bearing argument, such as partition double-counting, is required.
strengths: Correctly centers the variables and constructs an example with exactly \(136\) qualifying triples.
Correctly handles the case of exactly one positive term and obtains easy bounds when \(p\ge16\).

errors.description: The fixed-\(p\) construction in Case 2 only exhibits one distribution; it does not prove that arbitrary distributions have at least as many nonnegative triples.

Decreasing \(x_1\) can make triples containing it negative, which can reduce \(A\); merely noting that other positive entries may create additional triples does not quantify or prove the necessary compensation.
The statement that \(p=18\) implies all \(x_i=0\) conflicts with the definition of \(p\); in fact, \(p=18\) is impossible when the sum is zero.
